standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Introduced at the start of the counted proof (line 28161)

standard_prerequisites.name: Choice of a rapidly decreasing weight vector
standard_prerequisites.use: Makes each weight dominate all the later coordinates combined, which is what separates the values at distinct multi-indices.

core_obligations: For the finite set of multi-indices, define the constants A_i measuring the spread in the i-th coordinate (proof line 28161).
Choose the weights decreasing so fast that each weight exceeds the weighted sum of all later coordinates, which makes the first differing coordinate dominate (proof lines 28161-28162).

From a vanishing weighted difference, assume the first coordinate difference is nonnegative and derive a contradiction unless that difference is zero, then repeat down the coordinates to conclude the multi-indices agree (proof lines 28163-28177).
proof_roadmap: Measure the spread of the finite set of multi-indices coordinate by coordinate (proof lines 28159-28161).
Choose rapidly decreasing weights and separate the values by looking at the first coordinate where the multi-indices differ (proof lines 28161-28177).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for a finite set of multi-indices in n variables one can choose a weight vector, rapidly decreasing in its entries, such that the weighted sums separate the multi-indices (statement lines 28144-28157). The proof does not invoke a generic linear functional: it defines the coordinatewise spreads A_i, selects the weights so that each dominates the weighted sum of all later coordinates, and then, from a vanishing weighted difference, looks at the first coordinate where the multi-indices differ and derives a contradiction unless that difference is zero, descending through the coordinates (proof lines 28159-28177). The choice of how fast the weights decrease is exactly what makes that first coordinate decisive, and the author writes the inequality chain out. H2.
